narrativeSpine.why: A powerful maker cannot obtain a genuine encounter merely by making more predictable worlds; the reader is invited into a novel that puts speculative design under pressure from inhabitants.
narrativeSpine.how: The book combines a revisable table of speculative operations with fictional visits; a library scarcity shift and copying-in-time make its method tangible.
narrativeSpine.what: Readers gain a way to follow inventions into social consequences, and a story that tests what such classification misses; begin with the table explanation and first night.

artIdentity: An inhabited speculative workshop and tactile reading spaces; rich coral, teal, violet, amber foreground details, calm three-theme backgrounds, Red Hat Display/Text, concrete hands/eyes/grounded furniture. Four different scales and situations: workshop panorama, close library decision, domestic obligation across futures, reader-eye page-to-scene transition.

scenes.title: When a world can answer back
scenes.readerGain: Recognize why this work combines a novel with an atlas, and what the pairing offers beyond a catalogue of tropes.
scenes.composition: A wide, inhabited workshop panorama, seen diagonally at child height; Aster occupies one edge, the pupil occupies the other, and a projected rehearsal occupies the space between them. No repeated home icon or cosmic circles.
lines: Hunger After All the Worlds makes worldbuilding answer to its inhabitants.
This novel pairs encounters with an atlas of how speculative ideas work.
In the story, Aster builds worlds that no longer surprise her.
Her pupils explore inventions whose consequences resist a tidy classification.
Readers follow a changed rule into relationships, institutions, and lived costs.
The story then asks what even that careful method might miss.
beatActions: A pupil reaches toward a living model; an inhabitant turns toward the visitor instead of remaining an inert display figure. Establish two different agents with different purposes.
The workshop projection acquires a small removable analysis card attached to a specific changed mechanism, while the inhabitant continues an unfinished task.
A predicted gesture is rehearsed just ahead of the pupil’s actual gesture; Aster anticipates it with a tired, unsurprised expression. Keep prediction traces short and local, not decorative lines.
The pupil pauses instead of following the projected action; the prediction fades, and the inhabitant keeps their own appointment. No late revelation or explanation of the children’s hidden regions.
The model’s changed route forces its inhabitant to reschedule a meeting with another person. This is conceptual staging of the propagation test, not a named plot incident.
Aster withdraws the analytical overlay and looks directly at the pupil; the scene ends with attentive uncertainty, not a solved ethical lesson.
scenes.emotion: Curiosity → the unease of perfect prediction → relief when another agent remains irreducible.

scenes.title: Every book, one decision
scenes.readerGain: Understand a speculative operation through the actual library example: abundance moves scarcity from information to selection.
scenes.composition: A close, deep-perspective library aisle with a single reader, a real reading surface and many restrained book spines; the foreground desk and the reader’s hands dominate, not tiny shelves. Warm coral, teal and amber volumes against a calm background.
lines: Consider the book’s example of a library containing every possible book.
The information is abundant, but choosing what matters remains difficult.
Our reader still needs one useful selection before time runs out.
More available books do not automatically make that choice easier.
The atlas calls attention to this movement of scarcity.
It asks what a new possibility changes, rather than merely naming it.
beatActions: Shelves unfold deeper into the room while the same reader remains at the same desk. Books have believable spines, page blocks and proportioned covers, not zigzag polygons.
The reader compares two incompatible candidate pages and places both down; the stack of candidates grows while the chosen-reading place remains empty.
A visible clock advances once; the reader looks from the clock to the unsatisfied reading task. Narration says our reader to identify the staging as an illustrative example.
Another shelf opens, but the camera stays on the hands hesitating between candidates. Avoid frenetic motion; hold the unresolved choice.
A small diagram on the reader’s analysis slip names Scarcity shift beside a route from shelf abundance to the selection task; it labels the mechanism, not a second scene heading.

The reader places one book in the reading position while the unresolved alternatives remain visible. This demonstrates an actual decision with remaining uncertainty, not an all-purpose solution to selection.
scenes.emotion: Delight at abundance → decision pressure → focused, provisional choice.

scenes.title: A premise creates obligations
scenes.readerGain: See why combining operations produces social questions rather than just more exotic settings.
scenes.composition: An intimate domestic situation cut across two future moments. A shared earlier photograph and promise lie on a central table; two distinct future participants move toward different appointments. The supporting relation, rather than an abstract branching diagram, remains the focus.
lines: For example, copied minds can enter different branches of time.
Two people share a past, but their futures separate.
Which obligations travel with both, and which must change?
The atlas turns that unusual premise into a social question.
The novel adds inhabitants who can reject their visitors’ explanations.
Their deadlines and loyalties exceed whatever a convenient category records.
beatActions: The photograph and a commitment made before copying are shared; one remembered person becomes two present participants with matching earlier history.
The participants acquire visibly different calendar appointments and turn in different directions; use distinct props and gestures instead of merely tinting clones.
A person awaiting the earlier commitment addresses both participants; both look back, and neither is erased or automatically assigned the duty.
A visitor’s analysis note identifies the two interacting changes, Copying and Time; it remains smaller than the actual unresolved relationship.
The local participant holds up a hand to interrupt the visitor’s convenient classification, then points to the outstanding commitment.
The appointment time advances; the visitor lowers the note and listens. Preserve the unresolved choice and avoid inventing a resolution or named scene.
scenes.emotion: Wonder at branching → discomfort at inherited obligation → attention to the affected person.

scenes.title: Start with the first night
scenes.readerGain: Give a specific route into the book and a concrete way to read its paired forms.
scenes.composition: A reader’s-eye close view of two well-made bound sections on a reading table: one analytical and one narrative. A hand turns the page into the first workshop encounter; the camera follows the page into a scene detail, rather than returning to a generic house or presenting a wall of cards.
lines: Begin with Why a periodic table rather than a list of tropes.
Then enter The Room Where Surprise No Longer Existed.
Compare what the atlas names with what its inhabitants still dispute.
Its literary references let readers trace the traditions behind each encounter.
The reward is learning how inventions alter lives, not just landscapes.
The novel asks who gets to decide what those lives mean.
beatActions: The analysis section opens to one legible operation and its concrete consequence; retain page blocks and natural book geometry, with no tiny reproduced source table.
The reader turns to the named opening night; the chapter title belongs on the actual page, in a readable display hierarchy that does not compete with the player heading.
The camera focuses on a place where the visitor’s category and the inhabitant’s action differ; the paper analysis leaves deliberate space for revision.
One source attribution appears as a modest inscription in the memorial environment, with another origin visible only when the page moves. Do not present a parade of famous names as proof of quality.
The camera settles on the affected participant’s practical unfinished activity, now understandable through the two preceding examples.
The participant retains the next move; the reader’s hand rests ready to turn the page. Close on the invitation to continue, with no invented resolution.
scenes.emotion: Orientation → recognition of intellectual inheritance → curiosity with a clear next reading step.
